record.context_brief: Dichromatic number of a recursively built class
record.original_question: Let C be the class of digraphs generated by the following rules: the oriented graph K_2 belongs to C; adding a twin of a vertex of a graph in C keeps the graph in C; and gluing two members of C along at most two non-adjacent vertices again produces a member of C. Does every digraph in C have bounded dichromatic number, or can the dichromatic number in this class grow arbitrarily large?

evidence.quote: Build C a class of digraphs as follow : oriented K2 is in C , adding a twin to a vertex of a graph of C results in a graph of C and the graph obtained from two members of C glued on at most 2 non-adjacent vertices is a member of C .
Does the defined class have bounded dichromatic number ?

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is recorded as an open question from a 2023 workshop on digraphs. While related work on twin-distance-hereditary digraphs (Komander–Rehs, 2021/2023) shows that the dichromatic number is polynomial-time computable on related classes, no source found resolves whether the dichromatic number is bounded on the specific recursively defined class above. Status appears to remain open.
